run: 3:00 PM ET run (Sunday). The morning run didn't complete, so this run graded all of Saturday's tickets first. Picks focus on backup and tired goalies in tonight's NHL games, short-handed NBA rosters (unders and big cushions), Philadelphia's backup-QB start on Sunday night, and Monday soccer, NHL, NCAAB and tennis favorites. Every leg starts at 5:10 PM ET or later.

singles.market: New York Rangers Alt Total Goals
singles.reason: Edmonton is expected to start backup goalie Matt Tomkins on the road at Madison Square Garden. FanDuel prices the Rangers near 3.2 goals; a backup in goal makes 4+ more likely than the plus price says. NHL team totals have been one of our best angles (9-1 in the Best Shot tickets).

Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back with Johansson (.859 save percentage) expected in goal, and Anaheim's goaltending is also shaky. Tired legs plus an .859 goalie is the exact spot where team-total overs have hit for us, and +114 is a fair price for a home team facing that matchup.

singles.event: Los Angeles Clippers @ Golden State Warriors
singles.reason: Both rosters are badly short-handed, with Golden State missing most of its top rotation and the Clippers also thin. Losing the main creators slows the pace and lowers shot quality. NBA injury unders keep being our most reliable NBA angle, and 219.5 is still at plus money (+106).

parlays.name: Backup Goalie Team Totals
parlays.reason: Two team-total overs against weak or tired goaltending, one per game. Lesson applied: NHL team totals have been our strongest angle, safe parlays stay at 2-3 legs, and NHL overs are kept away from NBA overs.

legs.market: New York Rangers Alt Total Goals
legs.reason: Edmonton is expected to start backup goalie Matt Tomkins on the road at Madison Square Garden. The Rangers only need 3 goals against a backup at home.
Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back with Johansson (.859 save percentage) expected in goal, and Anaheim's goaltending is also shaky. Anaheim only needs 3 at home against a tired team.

parlays.name: Short-Handed Dogs With Cushion
parlays.reason: Big bought-up cushions on short-handed underdogs. Lesson applied: +3.5 on a short-handed dog is a coin flip, so each leg here gets 7.5 to 9.5 points of protection, and no spread is 12 or more.

legs.reason: The Lakers are favored by about 3. Toronto would have to lose by 10 or more, and the low-scoring pace from the injuries in this game keeps margins tighter.
Indiana is short-handed as well, so the Pacers aren't built to win by double digits. Brooklyn gets almost two possessions of cushion beyond the main spread.

legs.event: Los Angeles Clippers @ Golden State Warriors
legs.reason: The Warriors are missing most of their top rotation, so laying more than 7 with what's left is a lot to ask. The Clippers are close to a pick'em on the moneyline (+110).

parlays.name: Prime-Time Football Unders
parlays.reason: Two NFL unders tied to quarterback and offense limits. Lesson applied: lean on unders where injuries cap scoring, and keep it to two legs.

legs.reason: Philadelphia is starting backup QB Tanner McKee and has a thin receiver group, and its main team total is only 16.5. Going under 20.5 gives them room for two touchdowns and two field goals.
The main total sits in the mid-40s. Buying the under up to 50.5 means it only loses if both offenses break out on Monday night.

lottery.name: Best Shot $500K
lottery.reason: A $5 ticket on 25 legs, one per event, built from the most likely bought-down lines on a thin Sunday-Monday slate: NBA injury unders, backup-goalie NHL overs, the backup-QB SNF under, soccer double chances and under 2.5/3.5, Monday NHL puck lines, and big college and tennis favorites. There are no coin-flip moneylines under -150.

Edmonton is expected to start backup goalie Matt Tomkins on the road at Madison Square Garden, and Edmonton scores plenty itself.

history.name: Injury-Edge NBA Favorites
history.whyExplanation: Lost on one leg: Toronto lost 121-114 at home to Orlando. Miami and Detroit both won easily.
history.lesson: A short-priced home favorite is not safe just because of injury news. Orlando's healthy starters outscored Toronto in the first half. Check whether the underdog is fully healthy before using a -230 favorite as filler.

history.name: Unders Trio

legs.event: New Jersey Devils @ Vegas Golden Knights

history.whyExplanation: Lost two of three legs. Devils-Golden Knights went to 7 goals and Baylor-UCF finished at 50 (41-9), so a one-sided blowout still beat the under. Pistons-Nets under hit easily (204).
history.lesson: Unders in college football blowouts are risky because the favorite can score on its own. Use unders only where both offenses are weak. The NBA under based on pace and injuries was right.

history.name: 1st-Quarter Scorers
history.whyExplanation: Lost on one leg: Brunson scored only 2 first-quarter points because he was setting up teammates (two assists). Flagg had 12, Giannis 7, and Barnes and Garland 7 each.
history.lesson: Even -1200 legs miss. Five heavy favorites stacked together still lose about 1 time in 3 to 4. Use fewer legs, and avoid players whose first-quarter role is passing.

history.name: Injury-Usage Props Lottery

legs.event: Los Angeles Lakers @ Golden State Warriors

history.whyExplanation: Lost: 4 of 6 hit. Davis, Curry, McDaniels and Edgecombe hit. Cunningham had 5 rebounds and Barnes had 5, each missing by one.
history.lesson: Picking players who gain usage from injuries mostly worked (4-2). Rebound overs set right at the season average are close to coin flips, so pick props where the line is 1.5 or more below the player's recent average.

history.name: Notre Dame 1st Quarter -7.5

legs.actual: ND 7, Navy 3 after 1Q (won the quarter by 4)

history.whyExplanation: Lost. Notre Dame led only 7-3 after the first quarter. Navy kicked a field goal on its opening drive, and the Irish didn't take over until the second half (35-13 final, so the full-game read was right).
history.lesson: First-quarter spreads of 7 or more need a fast-starting offense AND an opponent that can't move the ball early. Service academies' ball-control offenses shorten the first quarter, so take the full game or 1H instead of a 1Q line against option teams.

history.name: Injury-Edge NBA Favorites
history.whyExplanation: WON at -109. Memphis beat Sacramento by 31, Portland won at Utah by 22, and San Antonio beat Minnesota by 10.

history.name: Goalie & Pace Overs
history.whyExplanation: Lost by one leg. Both NHL alt overs cashed at exactly 6 goals, but Hawks-Pelicans finished at 220, 13.5 short, because Atlanta's offense collapsed in a 22-point loss.
history.lesson: NBA overs can die when one side gets blown out; pair NHL pace overs with each other rather than with an NBA over that needs both teams to score.

history.name: QB-Injury Favorites
history.whyExplanation: Lost by one leg. Michigan (28-21) and Texas (31-3) won, but SMU lost 30-27 at Syracuse.
history.lesson: Road ACC favorites in close lines are too fragile; the QB-injury angle needs a home favorite or a clearly bigger talent gap.

history.name: Best Shot $500K
history.whyExplanation: Lost. 17 of 24 graded legs hit, but seven missed: Hawks ML (lost by 22), BYU -16.5 (won by 7), Nebraska ML, Argonauts ML (lost on a TD with 44 seconds left), Oklahoma State -9.5 (lost 51-49), Ohio State ML (lost 30-18 at USC).
history.lesson: Coin-flip road favorites (Ohio State at USC, Oklahoma State at Iowa State) and big CFB spreads (BYU -16.5) keep sinking long tickets. Road favorites in conference rivalries need cushion.

history.name: Heavy Favorites Ladder
history.whyExplanation: Lost by one leg. 18 of 19 favorites won; Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Dortmund, and a draw loses a 90-minute moneyline.
history.lesson: Avoid 90-minute soccer moneylines in derbies and top-of-table matches (Der Klassiker): the draw is ~25% even for a big favorite. Use 'Double Chance' or draw-no-bet style markets, or leave them out.

history.name: NHL Shooters Ladder

legs.event: St. Louis Blues @ Detroit Red Wings

history.whyExplanation: Lost. MacKinnon (5), Pastrnak (4), Thompson (8) and DeBrincat (3) hit, but Matthews, Celebrini and Caufield had 2 shots each and Robertson had 1.
history.lesson: 3+ shots on goal is closer to 55-65% for most stars, not 75%; eight of them stacked is a long shot. Use 2+ SOG for ladders, or only 3+ for players averaging 4+ shots.

history.name: 76ers @ Hornets Under 210.5 (Alt Total)
history.whyExplanation: Missed: PHI 109-104 = 213 total.
history.lesson: Charlotte and Philadelphia shot well late; 213 beat the injury-under by 2.5. Depleted rosters do not always mean slow pace.

history.name: Thunder @ Rockets Under 217.5 (Alt Total)

history.name: Clemson Team Total Under 20.5
history.whyExplanation: Missed: Clemson scored 36 (won 36-24).
history.lesson: Clemson's passing-game injuries were overrated; they scored 36. Team-total unders need a weak offense, not just a banged-up one.

history.name: Washington Team Total Under 19.5

history.lesson: Reasoning held up; keep this angle.

history.name: Goalie Mismatch NHL
history.whyExplanation: WON at +165. Montreal beat Pittsburgh 5-4 against weak goaltending, and Columbus-Dallas stayed at 4 goals, under 6.5.
history.lesson: The goalie-mismatch angle worked again; keep pairing a weak-goalie side with a cushion under.

history.name: Prime-Time CFB Favorites (Alt Lines)
history.whyExplanation: Lost. Missouri -4.5 hit easily (won by 24), but Florida State lost to Clemson 36-24 and Nebraska lost to Washington 17-10.
history.lesson: Buying down a near pick'em favorite (FSU -1.5, Nebraska -3.5) still leaves a coin-flip winner; alt lines only help when the favorite is clearly better. Washington's QB injury was overrated as an edge.

history.name: Short-Handed NBA Dogs (Alt Lines)
history.whyExplanation: Lost by one leg. Rockets +1.5 cashed (won by 21), but Charlotte lost by 5 and missed +3.5 by 1.5 points.
history.lesson: Taking points with a short-handed home dog against a short-handed favorite is close to a coin flip; buy more cushion (+5.5 or more) or skip.

legs.event: Jean Paul Lebosnoyani v Farman Hasanov

history.whyExplanation: WON at +1426. All nine favorites won: Szabova, Kropschot, Reese, Lebosnoyani, Luana Santos, Jacobe Smith, Piera Rodriguez, Sezinando and Shnaider (Tokyo final).

topLessons: Soccer: use Double Chance or goals markets, not 90-minute moneylines, in derbies and top matches (Bayern drew 2-2 and sank an 18-of-19 ladder).
NHL shots: 3+ SOG only for players averaging 4+ shots; use 2+ for ladders.
College alt spreads of -8.5 or more missed 4 of 7; avoid them and late-night G5 favorites.
NHL team totals and NBA injury unders went 9-1 in the Best Shot; build around them.
Buying down a pick'em favorite, or a short-handed dog at +3.5, is still a coin flip; get +5.5 or more cushion or skip.
Road conference favorites at coin-flip prices (Ohio State at USC, SMU at Syracuse) keep losing; use home favorites or cushion.
The 64%+ favorite filter is 9-for-9 in UFC; keep it for fight and tennis ladders.
Keep NBA overs apart from NHL overs in parlays; a blowout kills the NBA over.
Coin-flip moneylines (-110 to -150) killed the long tickets: 0-4 in the morning Best Shot. Lottery legs need ~75%+ true probability.
Big NBA spreads (-12 or more) are fragile in garbage time: Celtics -15.5 won by 14 and missed twice.
Do not carry a failed-risk leg into multiple tickets; correlated reuse turned one miss into three losses (Kent St, Kraken, Celtics, Lakers).
Pace/goalie-driven overs and injury-usage unders/props were the best angles (Overs parlay won +599; singles 2nd run 5-1).
